config.title: Polling Hook

intro.title: Polling Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Angular hook that automatically fetches data from an API at regular intervals, known as polling. You'll learn how to use Angular's built-in RxJS Observables and the `interval` function to create timed data updates. The main technologies involved are Angular services, TypeScript, and reactive programming with RxJS operators like `switchMap`. By the end, you'll have a reusable polling hook that can be integrated into any Angular component to display live-updating data.
intro.usecase: A polling hook is essential for building real-time dashboards and live data feeds in applications like financial trading platforms, live sports score trackers, or collaborative project management tools. Developers use this pattern to periodically fetch updated data from a server, such as stock prices, delivery statuses, or team notifications, without requiring manual user refreshes. This ensures users always see the latest information, enhancing interactivity and responsiveness in features like live charts, activity logs, or status panels.

objectives: Implement a custom Angular hook that manages polling logic
Configure polling intervals and control start/stop behavior
Initialize reactive state to track polling data and status
Integrate the polling hook with a component to fetch live data
Manipulate polling parameters dynamically based on user input
Render real-time updates from the polling hook in the UI
Bind error handling and loading states to the polling lifecycle

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and RxJS utilities
steps.instruction: Import Component, Injectable, OnInit, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core', and import interval, Subject, takeUntil, and switchMap from 'rxjs'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you need from their respective packages. Remember to use curly braces for named imports.

steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular core modules and RxJS utilities are imported, setting up the foundation for creating a polling hook.
successCriteria: Component, Injectable, OnInit, and OnDestroy are imported from '@angular/core', and interval, Subject, takeUntil, and switchMap are imported from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required modules, but not all. Check that you have Component, Injectable, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and interval, Subject, takeUntil, switchMap from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component, Injectable, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and interval, Subject, takeUntil, switchMap from 'rxjs'.

steps.title: Create a data service with polling capability
steps.instruction: Create a new service class called PollingService and decorate it with @Injectable() to make it injectable throughout your Angular application.
steps.hint: In Angular, services are typically created as classes with the @Injectable() decorator. This decorator marks the class as one that can be injected as a dependency.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required Angular and RxJS modules here

// Create your PollingService class with @Injectable decorator below
steps.expectedOutcome: A PollingService class is created and decorated with @Injectable(), ready to contain polling logic in subsequent steps.
successCriteria: The PollingService class exists and is decorated with @Injectable()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both created the PollingService class AND added the @Injectable() decorator above it. Both are required for this step.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PollingService class with @Injectable() decorator wasn't created correctly. Please create a class named PollingService and add @Injectable() above it.

steps.title: Add private properties to the polling service
steps.instruction: Inside your PollingService class, add a private Subject property named 'destroy$' and a public Observable property named 'data$'.
steps.hint: Use RxJS Subject and Observable types. The destroy$ Subject will be used to clean up subscriptions, and data$ will emit the polled data.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your PollingService will have internal state properties ready for implementing polling logic.
successCriteria: The PollingService class contains a private destroy$ Subject and a public data$ Observable property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both properties: a private destroy$ Subject and a public data$ Observable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PollingService should include a private destroy$ Subject and a public data$ Observable property. Review the RxJS Subject and Observable types.

steps.title: Implement polling logic in the service
steps.instruction: In the PollingService class, create a public method named startPolling that returns an Observable of string. Inside this method, use the RxJS interval operator to emit every 2 seconds, switchMap to call a mock API function, and takeUntil to stop when destroy$ emits.
steps.hint: Remember to import interval and switchMap from 'rxjs' if not already done. The method signature should be: startPolling(): Observable<string>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PollingService now has a startPolling method that creates a polling stream using RxJS operators.
successCriteria: The startPolling method is defined with correct return type, uses interval(2000), switchMap with a mock API call (e.g., of('Mock data')), and takeUntil(this.destroy$).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your method uses all required operators: interval, switchMap, and takeUntil.
steps.feedbackWrong: The startPolling method is missing or doesn't use the required RxJS operators correctly. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Add cleanup method to the polling service
steps.instruction: Add a public method named stopPolling to the PollingService that completes the destroy$ Subject to clean up subscriptions.
steps.hint: Define a method that calls next() and complete() on the destroy$ Subject.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PollingService now has a stopPolling method that properly cleans up subscriptions by completing the destroy$ Subject.
successCriteria: The PollingService contains a public stopPolling method that calls next() and complete() on the destroy$ Subject.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your stopPolling method calls both next() and complete() on the destroy$ Subject.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stopPolling method is missing or doesn't properly clean up the subscription. It should complete the destroy$ Subject.

steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and a basic template that includes a heading.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. The template can be a simple string with an <h1> element.

steps.title: Inject the polling service into the component
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, add a constructor that injects the PollingService as a dependency.
steps.hint: Use the constructor parameter with the service type to enable dependency injection.
steps.analogousExample:
// Injecting a service in Angular
constructor(private myService: MyService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a constructor that receives the PollingService instance.
successCriteria: AppComponent has a constructor with a PollingService parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the constructor parameter is properly typed with PollingService.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should accept a PollingService parameter to enable dependency injection.

steps.title: Initialize component properties for polling data
steps.instruction: Add a public property named polledData to the AppComponent class to store the polling results, and a private property named subscription to manage the polling subscription.
steps.hint: Declare polledData as a string (or the type you expect from the service) and subscription as a Subscription type. You'll need to import Subscription from 'rxjs'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have polledData and subscription properties declared, ready to store data from the polling service.
successCriteria: AppComponent has a polledData property of type string and a private subscription property of type Subscription.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added one property, but you need both polledData and subscription. Make sure subscription is private.
steps.feedbackWrong: The properties are not correctly declared. Add polledData: string and private subscription: Subscription to the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Implement component initialization with polling
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, implement the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to subscribe to the polling service's data$ observable and store the received data in the polledData property.
steps.hint: Use the ngOnInit method to start polling when the component initializes. Subscribe to data$ and assign the emitted value to this.polledData.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will now automatically start receiving polled data when it initializes, storing it in the polledData property.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method is implemented, subscribes to pollingService.data$, and updates polledData with the emitted values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've implemented the ngOnInit method and subscribed to pollingService.data$ to update polledData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component initialization isn't complete. You need to implement ngOnInit to subscribe to the polling service and store the data.

steps.title: Add component cleanup to prevent memory leaks
steps.instruction: Implement the ngOnDestroy lifecycle hook in the AppComponent to unsubscribe from the polling service and stop polling.
steps.hint: Add the ngOnDestroy method inside the AppComponent class. Inside it, call this.subscription.unsubscribe() and this.pollingService.stopPolling().
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have an ngOnDestroy method that properly cleans up subscriptions and stops the polling service.
successCriteria: ngOnDestroy method is implemented with both this.subscription.unsubscribe() and this.pollingService.stopPolling() calls.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngOnDestroy, but make sure to include both cleanup actions: unsubscribe from the subscription and stop the polling service.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnDestroy method is missing or incomplete. Add the ngOnDestroy lifecycle hook with both cleanup actions.
